Are you experienced in continuing airworthiness management and motivated by ensuring safe, efficient and reliable aircraft operations? Do you have strong leadership skills, a technical mindset and an interest in optimizing maintenance planning, costs and processes?

Then you may be our new Continuing Airworthiness Management Organisation (CAMO) Manager.

As CAMO Manager at JoinJet, you will have an exciting and responsible position with a key role in ensuring the continued airworthiness of our aircraft fleet. You will be responsible for planning and following up on maintenance activities and for ensuring that our aircraft are maintained to the highest standards, enabling safe and efficient operations.

You will also be responsible for ensuring that the applicable rules and regulations are implemented and maintained within JoinJet’s CAMO and that the organisation remains compliant with its CAME.

Your responsibilities

Your main tasks and areas of responsibility will include:

· Overseeing all standard continuing airworthiness management functions

· Managing and maintaining the technical documentation for all aircraft

· Responsible for long-term maintenance planning and budgeting

· Ensuring efficient maintenance planning and minimizing aircraft downtime

· Driving LEAN initiatives and continuous improvement of CAMO processes

· Maintaining the technical dialogue with aviation authorities

· Ensuring that the aircraft remain airworthy and compliant with all applicable technical and regulatory requirements

· Monitoring and optimizing maintenance costs and aircraft utilization

· Leading and developing the CAMO team

· Acting as the technical point of contact for relevant internal and external stakeholders

· Performing ad hoc tasks and projects related to CAMO and technical operations

The position reports to the Accountable Manager and works closely with JoinJet and SUN-AIR Technic on technical and operational matters.

Expectations

You have experience from a similar position with management responsibility and at least five years of relevant experience, preferably with at least two years in an administrative or management position within the aviation industry.

You have a solid understanding of airworthiness, maintenance and quality systems and are comfortable using IT as an integral part of your daily work. You have broad technical knowledge and practical experience from aviation, combined with a structured and business-oriented approach.

As the Nominated Postholder for CAMO, you will have overall leadership responsibility for the CAMO department.

A background as an aircraft technician is an advantage.

As a person

You are a natural leader who motivates and develops your employees through trust, clear communication and delegation. You have good interpersonal skills and enjoy working collaboratively across departments.

You are not afraid to challenge existing processes and look for better and more efficient ways of working. You are solution-oriented, structured and take pride in delivering high-quality work.

You have a good sense of humour and contribute positively to the working environment. You have a basic understanding of finance and a sound commercial mindset.

You are proficient in Microsoft Office and communicate confidently in both Danish and English, verbally and in writing.

Some travel activity should be expected in the position, although it will be limited.

Please note that you must have a residence and work permit that allows you to live and work in Denmark.

We offer

We offer an exciting and challenging position in an international business aviation company, where you will have the opportunity to develop both professionally and personally.

You will become part of an experienced team and have the opportunity to take an active role in the continued development of our CAMO organisation and the business as a whole.

We also offer:

· A responsible and varied full-time position

· An international working environment

· Excellent office facilities and canteen

· Competitive salary according to qualifications

· Pension scheme

· Opportunities for professional and personal development

How to apply

If you find the position interesting, we would be pleased to hear from you.

Please send us your application and CV through the application link as soon as possible. Applications are accepted in both Danish and English.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact us on +45 76 500 100.

We look forward to welcoming you on board JoinJet.

Fly the way you like.

JoinJet is headquartered in Billund and arranges individual flights for, for example, VIPs, companies, bands, sports clubs, etc. JoinJet also manages private and commercial aircraft, as well as aircraft sales and leasing and FBO service, which are part of JoinJet's business areas. With over 30 years of experience, the company understands the diverse needs of its customers, and its products are tailored to meet those needs. JoinJet always focuses on quality and precision. JoinJet is part of the Sundberg Aviation Group, and from the headquarters in Billund, the group's business areas are managed, which today include air ambulance service worldwide, corporate shuttles, aircraft maintenance, spare parts sales, charter flights, as well as international aircraft sales and leasing.

Are you ready to unlock your potential in system engineering at a world leading technology driven company?

We can offer an exciting opportunity where you get to use your technical skills in an innovative environment, with the aim to push the performance of radars to the limit. At Weibel, you will join a global, technology-driven company that develops and produces state-of-the-art radar systems. Our biggest asset is our talented employees, and we believe that by fostering open and curious discussions, we can achieve the best possible solutions.

We are now looking for a new colleague for our Systems Engineering team who wants to be a part of developing our advanced radar systems.

About the position

As a System Engineer in Weibel you will work with requirements and configuration of the overall system. This requires close collaboration with our different engineering departments to ensure that the various sub-systems work together in a manner that fulfills the overall system requirements.

Working at Weibel will provide you with hands-on experience with our radars. You get an understanding of the physics limiting radar performance and potential solutions.

You are a part of the project from the final stages of the sales process until the factory acceptance test with the costumer, where the performance of the finished system is tested based on the predefined requirements.

The position will include tasks such as:

• Drive product definitions and requirements in collaboration with project managers and sub-system engineers.

• Take the technical leadership in a project by bringing people from different departments together, leading internal review meetings etc.

• Participate in internal project meetings and technical meetings with the customer as responsible for system design.

• Assist the project manager to prepare material for design reviews with the customer and to find answers to technical questions.

• Provide technical support to our sales team during project bid-phases.

We do not expect you to have experience with radar systems beforehand, but it is an advantage. You will work in close collaboration with our experienced System Engineers, who have a deep understanding of our systems and you can look forward to a steep learning curve.

You can expect 10-20 travelling days per year.

About our new colleague

You have a university degree within a relevant engineering discipline and you are fluent in English – both spoken and written. You have a few years of experience from a similar organization where you have worked with design, verification and test of complex systems. You have a strong technical foundation and some knowledge of system engineering.

You will play an important role in ensuring that the development of the different sub-systems follow the overall requirements for the system. Therefore, if you are to be successful it is important that you work in a systematic manner and have the ability to keep the overall requirements in mind.

You will work with many difference stakeholders, so it is key that you have good communication skills and the ability to present your results in an effective and structured manner. You take ownership of your own tasks and deliver according to deadlines and the agreed upon quality.

Your new team

You will be joining a team of highly competent and enthusiastic colleagues. The level of experience in the team spans from newly graduated to more than 30 years of experience. Our team members have very different educational backgrounds that varies from electrical, aerospace and mechanical engineering to physics and computer science. We have created it in this way, because we believe that bringing people with different competences together will generate the best solutions.

What we offer

By joining Weibel, you will become part of a professional high-tech company with a dynamic environment who are market leaders in its field. It is a unique opportunity to join the company at an exciting stage.

Contact and application

Please apply at our website using the ”Apply” button. If you have any questions, you are very welcome to contact Engineering Manager, Lina Klintberg, likl@weibel.dk

We will be holding interviews on an ongoing basis during the application period and may close the position before the application deadline. Therefore, please send us your application at your earliest convenience.

The deadline is the 23rd of October 2026.

Please note that this position requires a criminal record with no remarks and the ability to obtain a security clearance.

We are looking forward to hearing from you.

Become part of a Danish company

Weibel Scientific A/S is a Danish-owned engineering company experiencing strong growth. We develop and manufacture high‑technology radar systems for use in areas such as space research, aviation, defense, and the protection of critical infrastructure. We are a world leader in the development of Doppler radars and, since our establishment in 1977, we have delivered more than 4,500 state‑of-the-art radar systems to over 40 countries.

Our headquarters are located in Allerød and employ nearly 600 people.

At Weibel, you can look forward to an exciting and challenging position in a dynamic and forward‑looking company with in-house production and advanced technological development.

Read more about us on our website.
